seats.oldValue: That he liked the big house he had taken.
seats.newValue: That he hoped to see them, and had heard they were beautiful.
seats.execution: Lines 5 and 6 say Mr Bingley 'had entertained hopes of being admitted to a sight of the young ladies, of whose beauty he had heard much'. That is inside the window, but it is what he hoped and had heard, not what the daughters found out. From the upper window at lines 7 and 8 they learned only that he wore a blue coat and rode a black horse.

seats.oldValue: His two sisters and both their husbands.
seats.newValue: His two sisters, the husbands of both the sisters, and one other young man.
seats.execution: One detail changed from line 22, which names only 'the husband of the eldest'; this option gives both sisters a husband. Lines 21 and 22 say the party 'consisted of only five altogether', so a second husband would make six.

seats.oldValue: The way a person speaks to other people.
seats.newValue: A person's manners, and how pleasant they are.
seats.execution: Lines 24 and 25 put the word in a pair: 'a pleasant countenance, and easy, unaffected manners'. The child glosses 'countenance' with the other half of the pair, manners, and keeps the 'pleasant' beside it. Lines 31 to 34 keep the two apart for Mr Darcy too: 'his manners gave a disgust' is one fault and his 'disagreeable countenance' another.

seats.oldValue: Because he danced with lots of different ladies.
seats.newValue: Because he was so lively, and because he danced with lots of different ladies.
seats.execution: Both halves are Mr Bingley's, carried across to Mr Darcy: line 37 says Mr Bingley 'was lively and unreserved, danced every dance'. Mr Darcy dances only twice, at lines 39 and 40. Lines 27 to 29 give what drew the room: his 'fine, tall person, handsome features, noble mien' and the report of 'ten thousand a year'.

seats.oldValue: He complained that the ball had ended too early.
seats.newValue: He was angry, complaining that the ball had ended far too early.
seats.execution: Line 37 gives this to Mr Bingley, who 'was angry that the ball closed so early', and the child carries it across to Mr Darcy. Lines 31 to 33 give what changed the room: 'his manners gave a disgust', as he was found 'to be proud, to be above his company'.

seats.oldValue: Two: one with Miss Bingley and one with Elizabeth.
seats.newValue: Two: one with Miss Bingley and one with Elizabeth Bennet.
seats.execution: One name changed: Elizabeth Bennet for Mrs Hurst. Line 40 has Mr Darcy dance 'once with Mrs. Hurst and once with Miss Bingley'. Elizabeth sits out two dances at line 47, and Mr Darcy turns her down at lines 66 and 67.

seats.oldValue: Mr Darcy had refused to dance with her.
seats.newValue: Mr Darcy was standing near and would not dance with her.
seats.execution: Line 48 does have Mr Darcy 'standing near enough for her to' overhear, but line 47 has Elizabeth already sitting down 'by the scarcity of gentlemen'. His refusal comes at lines 65 to 67, while she is sitting, so the child gives a later event as the cause of an earlier one.

seats.oldValue: She wants her friends to feel sorry for her.
seats.newValue: She wants her friends to feel sorry for her after how badly she was treated.
seats.execution: A wish for sympathy is supplied. Mr Darcy's slight at lines 66 to 68 is real, but lines 71 to 73 say she told the story 'with great spirit' because she 'delighted in anything ridiculous', which is the opposite of asking for pity.

seats.oldValue: Anything going to the charity collection.
seats.newValue: Anything going to the charity collection on Friday.
seats.execution: Takes the right instruction block but the wrong container: lines 8 and 9 send everything with no name to the second box, going to 'the charity collection on Friday morning'. Line 9 says the bin bag 'was for anything with the sole coming off it'.

seats.oldValue: Both show he agrees with Ilya's plans.
seats.newValue: Both are about Whitby and Ilya's group, not the lockers.
seats.execution: Whitby and the group are inside the window but belong to the other speaker: they are Ilya's subject at lines 19 and 20. Reuben's two replies are about the sorting: 'These are all size nine' at line 17, and the swimming hat at lines 21 and 22.

seats.oldValue: They are sorted again at the school on Friday.
seats.newValue: They go to shops in Leeds, then to a warehouse.
seats.execution: Built from lines 24 and 25 in the wrong order. Miss Bhatt says 'A warehouse', then 'Leeds, she thought, or somewhere near it, and then out to shops all over the place.' The bags reach the warehouse first and the shops after, and the shops are all over the place rather than in Leeds.

seats.oldValue: He could not tell whose the jumper was, so he put it in the box.
seats.newValue: He did not know the jumper was his until Miss Bhatt found the name.
seats.execution: Line 31 says Reuben 'knew before he turned the collar out whose it was', from the shape of his mum's capitals. Miss Bhatt only finds the collar at lines 44 and 45, after he has put the jumper in the Friday box knowing it was his. The child gives him the very doubt the passage rules out.

seats.oldValue: Read it and then put it away again.
seats.newValue: Opened it and then put it back in his pocket.
seats.execution: Lines 35 and 36 say he 'looked at the edge of it and put it back without opening it'. The child keeps the putting back and drops the 'without', so the paper is opened.

seats.oldValue: Reuben has already written his name on it.
seats.newValue: Reuben has not signed it because the sheet is already full.
seats.execution: Lines 38 and 39 say the sheet has eleven names and 'plenty of room left at the bottom', so it is not full. The child keeps the true half, that Reuben has not signed, and gives it a reason the passage denies.

seats.oldValue: Miss Bhatt wants it done before Friday.
seats.newValue: They can do it on Monday after spellings.
seats.execution: One detail changed: at line 41 Ilya says they can do the cupboard on Monday 'and get out of spellings', so it takes the place of spellings. The child keeps Monday and turns missing spellings into doing the cupboard after them.

seats.oldValue: She is waiting for him to say sorry for the mistake.
seats.newValue: She thinks he made a mistake, and waits for him to say sorry.
seats.execution: Invents a demand. At line 47 Reuben gives his reason, 'It won't fit me next year', and at lines 48 and 49 she folds the jumper 'the way he had folded it' and shuts the box, waiting for nothing from him.

seats.oldValue: He wanted to keep the cardigan for himself.
seats.newValue: He would rather keep the cardigan for himself than give it back.
seats.execution: Lines 13 and 14 have him 'put it in the returns box anyway', not keep it. The child gives him a wish the passage never states, and one his action contradicts.

seats.oldValue: Put it in the returns box, because it had a name in it.
seats.newValue: Put it in the returns box, low down, and pushed it flat.
seats.execution: Line 33 says he put it 'in the Friday box, low down', the box going to the charity collection, and line 34 that he 'pushed it flat'. The child keeps how he did it and changes the box to the returns box, which named things go in at lines 7 and 8 and which the passage says he did not use here.

seats.oldValue: It called out that it knew Marley.
seats.newValue: It cried out loud that it knew Marley.
seats.execution: Lines 69 and 70 say the flame leaped up 'as though it cried, "I know him; Marley's Ghost!"'. The 'as though' makes it a picture of the flame, and the child gives it a real voice.

seats.oldValue: The little station was too small for so many people.
seats.newValue: The little station was not big enough for so many people.
seats.execution: A likely enough complaint about a small wayside station, but lines 11 to 16 never say it. Watson's surprise at lines 12 to 14 is at 'two soldierly men in dark uniforms' with rifles in 'a sweet, simple country spot'.

seats.oldValue: Old gabled houses among the thick green foliage.
seats.newValue: Old gabled houses, peeping out from the green foliage.
seats.execution: True at lines 17 and 18, where 'old gabled houses peeped out from amid the thick green foliage', and part of the sunlit country rather than behind it. Line 19 gives what rose behind it: 'the long, gloomy curve of the moor'.

seats.oldValue: That they might take him in and dry him.
seats.newValue: That he was not choked, only half dead.
seats.execution: The words of line 15 with the two halves swapped: the big man 'said he was not dead but half choked'. The child keeps 'not', 'half', 'dead' and 'choked' and loses which one goes with which.

seats.oldValue: The family would go on feeding him if he stayed.
seats.newValue: The family would keep on feeding him raw meat if he stayed.
seats.execution: A bargain the lines never give him. Line 25 says he 'liked it immensely', but lines 28 and 29 give his own reason: 'There are more things to find out about in this house'.

seats.oldValue: It was large and only half looked after.
seats.newValue: It was a large garden and only half looked after.
seats.execution: Reuses lines 41 and 42, 'a large garden, only half cultivated', and describes the garden rather than saying what it means to him. Line 44 gives that: 'This is a splendid hunting-ground'.

seats.oldValue: Somebody more strange than Darzee.
seats.newValue: Somebody odd, who is more strange than Darzee.
seats.execution: Built from 'strange' plus the ending -er, as if the word meant more strange. At line 54 Rikki-tikki says 'I am a stranger here' and asks who Nag is: he is new to the place, not odd.

seats.oldValue: Because they had already told him about the baby.
seats.newValue: Because they had already told him what happened to the baby.
seats.execution: True at lines 52 and 53, before the hiss came: 'One of our babies fell out of the nest yesterday and Nag ate him.' The child answers from the earlier talk, but lines 55 and 56 give the hiss from the grass as the reason they say nothing.

seats.oldValue: Miss Deller said nobody was to open the net except her.
seats.newValue: Miss Deller said, on Monday, that nobody but her could open the net.
seats.execution: Reuses line 12, 'Miss Deller did say nobody was to open the net except her. She said it on Monday', and repeats her rather than saying what he does with it. Lines 13 and 14 give that: 'by Thursday the instruction is basically out of date'.

seats.oldValue: A lunchbox would keep them warm on the way.
seats.newValue: The governors tell him not to carry the net.
seats.execution: Nothing in lines 17 to 20 has the governors tell him anything. Line 20 says 'Nobody tells me the governors are in the hall', so he does not know they are there. Line 17 gives the reason he uses the lunchbox: 'The net will not carry flat'.

seats.oldValue: They had to sit down and have a drink of water.
seats.newValue: They sit down on the PE bench, and each have a long drink of water.
seats.execution: True at line 25 of Miss Deller, who 'sits down on the PE bench and has a long drink of water', carried across to Reception. Line 26 gives what Dilan says of Reception: 'Reception are fine.'

seats.oldValue: That two of them are up on the beam.
seats.newValue: That two of them are up on the beam over the stage where the ropes hang.
seats.execution: True at line 29, 'Two are up on the beam over the stage where the ropes hang', and Dilan's own account of where they are. What Mr Okafor says, at lines 29 and 30, is that 'nobody is going up there for a butterfly, not today'.

seats.oldValue: His mother came at half past two.
seats.newValue: His mother arrived at half past two, which is early for her.
seats.execution: True at line 36, 'She came at half past two, which is early for her', and a fact about his mother rather than his explanation. Line 39 gives that: the word 'again' 'will be about the fountain, and the fountain was ages ago'.

redrafts.value: He wants to keep them hidden from the teachers.
redrafts.execution: A plan no line gives him. Line 17 gives the reason for the lunchbox, 'The net will not carry flat', and at lines 18 and 19 two more ride openly on his sleeve 'the whole way'.

redrafts.value: His mother has promised not to raise the fountain.
redrafts.execution: A promise the lines never give her. At lines 36 and 37 she says nothing on the way past, only 'a small nod'. Line 39 gives his own explanation of 'again': 'that will be about the fountain, and the fountain was ages ago'.
